title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for parallel multi-tool calls with result injection & retries
author: Priya Reddy
description:
Motivation: improve ergonomics and robustness of tool/function calling when multiple tools are invoked in parallel from a single model response. This PR addresses three recurring pain points: (1) deterministic result injection order when tools complete out-of-order, (2) configurable retry semantics with idempotency to handle flaky tool endpoints, and (3) streaming stability when tool results are injected mid-stream (OpenAI compatibility and structured-output scenarios).

Summary of changes: added a parallel executor for tool calls that supports configurable priorities and deterministic injection points, introduced a retry policy layer with idempotency tokens and backoff strategies, and updated the streaming path to buffer/serialize injected results safely for both the Redwood and OpenAI-compat layers. Changed the public API surface minimally: new optional execution hints on the tool-calling payload (execution_mode, retry_policy, injection_strategy). Default behavior preserves previous synchronous/serial semantics to maintain backward compatibility.

Key behaviour and rationale: - Parallel tool calls are scheduled by the new executor which records logical call order and priority. Actual network completions can be out of order, but injection into the model response stream follows deterministic ordering rules (priority -> request_index -> completion_time) to avoid surprising interleavings. - Injection strategies: "merge" (merge key-value results into a single structured object), "sequential" (inject as separate tool messages preserving order), and "placeholder" (emit placeholders into the stream and replace once results arrive). The default is "merge" for structured-output endpoints. - Retries: retry_policy supports attempts, initial_backoff_ms, max_backoff_ms, and strategies (fixed, exponential). Retries are idempotent by design: callers can provide an idempotency_token or we generate one per execution to avoid duplicate side-effects. - Streaming: to preserve streaming stability we buffer injected data until we can emit a consistent update point; if a tool call fails after retries, we emit a structured failure message instead of partial payload to avoid downstream parse errors. - OpenAI-compatible layer: the compatibility shim now accepts the new execution hints and translates them to internal executor instructions; clients using OpenAI-style tool_call fields will see matching semantics. Documentation updates and SDK bindings are included for Python/TS SDKs.

Compatibility and migration notes: - No breaking changes by default; existing calls that do not set execution hints continue to behave serially. - Teams that want parallel behavior must opt-in by setting execution_mode: "parallel". - When enabling parallel+retries with external side-effecting tools, callers must supply idempotency_token or ensure their tool endpoints are idempotent.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests covering executor ordering, injection strategies and retry backoff logic. - Integration tests exercising streaming + injection against the OpenAI-compat shim and Redwood API. - Load-tested a synthetic workload of 10k parallel tool calls to validate latency and memory characteristics; added a perf canary job that compares latency percentiles pre/post.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation of parallel executor + deterministic ordering
- [x] Retry middleware with idempotency tokens
- [x] Streaming injector with placeholder/merge/sequential strategies
- [x] OpenAI-compat shim translation and tests
- [x] SDK examples and docs
- [x] Perf canary and CI coverage

Commits summary: - feat(tool-exec): add parallel tool executor with priority queue - feat(tool-exec): deterministic injection ordering and strategies - feat(retries): add retry middleware and idempotency token support - feat(streaming): buffer + inject tool results into streaming path safely - docs(tooling): add execution hints docs and SDK examples - test: add unit/integration tests for executor and backoff behaviors - perf: add canary job and summary metrics

Files changed (high-level): src/service/tool_executor.rs, src/service/retry_middleware.rs, src/service/streaming_injector.rs, src/api/openai_compat.rs, src/api/handlers/tool_call_handler.rs, sdk/python/redwood/tooling.py, sdk/ts/src/tooling.ts, docs/guides/tool-calling.md, tests/integration/tool_exec_parallels.rs, tests/unit/retry_policy.rs, .github/workflows/tooling-ci.yml, perf/canary/tool-calls.yaml, CHANGELOG.md

Rationale notes for reviewers: - Kept public API minimal (three new optional hints) to reduce churn. - Chose deterministic ordering rules to avoid surprising nondeterministic output which caused multiple downstream parsing bugs. - Introduced idempotency tokens rather than attempting to infer idempotency from payloads.

Merge outcome: merged via squash after green CI and two approvals.

If you want to try it locally: curl -X POST /v1/call_tool -d '{"model": "rwd-large", "input": "...", "tools": [...], "execution_mode": "parallel", "retry_policy": {"attempts":3}}' (OpenAI-compat accepts execution hints under tool_call.execution hints as well).

Marcos Li: Concern about memory usage when buffering for placeholder strategy under high concurrency. Can we cap buffer size per-execution and fall back to sequential emission?

release_notes: Improved tool-calling ergonomics: opt-in parallel execution, deterministic result injection strategies (merge/sequential/placeholder), idempotent retries with backoff, and streaming stability enhancements. See docs/guides/tool-calling.md for migration notes.
